name: a calendar view last looked at before a created claim's grace sync never makes it NOT_FOUND; a fresh one can
notes: §6.1 v1.10: a gcal.event entry counts towards full coverage for a calendar.* claim only if its lastSyncAt ≥ end(p,t) + graceMin; any other overlapping entry is capped with coverage.changes_unfollowed. A view looked at before the claimed event could have been created cannot say it never was (Hard Rule 5). A capped entry still counts for grace and still lets the row it saw verify.

Coverage (acct-a, every calendar, bound by the grant): the October view [10-01 00:00, 11-01 00:00], followed since 09:00 and last synced 14:00, when the user switched to November; the November view [11-01 00:00, 12-01 00:00], first looked at 14:35 (changesSince 14:35) and last synced 14:40.

c1: muse says at 14:02 (minute) it created 'Q4 planning' (targetAt 10-15 10:00). Window [10-12 10:00, 10-18 10:00]; end(p,t) + graceMin = 14:03 + 30 = 14:33. The only entry overlapping the window is the October view, synced 14:00 < 14:33 → capped. Coverage partial; no candidate (match.none). Rules: no_coverage no (partial); verified, partial no; pending no: graceElapsed reads any eligible gcal.event entry, and the November view synced 14:40 ≥ 14:33; partial_coverage → UNVERIFIABLE. PENDING until end + finalizeUnverifiableHours = 10-07 14:03. Reasons coverage.partial, coverage.changes_unfollowed (both {source: gcal.event}), match.none.
Under v1.9 the October view was full coverage of c1 and c1 was NOT_FOUND, FINAL: a false NOT_FOUND from a view looked at two minutes before the claim (Hard Rule 5).
